Two small things :
1) Goodyear welted boots are easier and less expensive to resole.
2) You can resole a GY welted boot more times. You can also replace a welt when it wears out, ( more than once possibly) but when a stich down is worn out from resoling, it's toast.

4:19 It's hotly debated whether stitchdown or Goodyear Welt is better and actually GYW is going to get you better water resistance most of the time. Stitchdown is usually (but not all the time) associated with cheaper-made footwear.

Hi, Michael. I've been watching your videos quite a lot recently, having enjoyed your work with Theo & Harris. In short, I've learned so much about clothing and fashion -- something I feel like I should know more about, being a man of... <ahem>... middle age. Thank you for that!

Prior to watching your videos, my comfortable go-to was a pair of blue jeans and a black t-shirt. Specifically, LL Bean t-shirts (small) and Levi's 505s (30x34). They look good, they're reasonably durable, and they fit. I have four pairs of jeans and 10 t-shirts. I literally wear nothing else because we live in California and I generally don't need to. My wife thinks it's "cute."

Having said that, being inspired by your videos, I was ready to at least think about spending money on nicer shirts and Japanese pants. Then I saw one particular video (forget which one it was) in which you were wearing jeans and a black t-shirt throughout. And I thought: "that just looks so great." And it made me happy and not want to spend a ton of money.

Not really sure what the point of this is. I really do appreciate your work and enjoy these videos. The boots might get me one day. I really like nice boots. Thanks again!
My only regret with these boots are not sizing wider

I have a pair of 11877s.  Same boot as the 877.  It's just a different color.  They are amazing work boots.  They are designed for iron workers.  Not having a heel prevents you from tripping.  They are also amazing on asphalt, concrete, or most flatter surfaces.  In my opinion, they aren't great hiking/outdoor boots.  The soles aren't that grippy on inclines or loose dirt.  I have a pair of Daner Pronghorns for hiking. 

Honestly, if you wear 11877s for construction, ironwork, or some other trade, they are amazing. I would rather wear my Danner Pronghorns for hiking, hunting, etc.
